target.title: fix(config): key agentDir collisions by volume case sensitivity
target.body:
Closes #105194

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users with case-sensitive macOS APFS or Windows NTFS volumes would hit a false `DuplicateAgentDirError` startup rejection when two agents used distinct `agentDir` paths that differed only by case, even though the filesystem treats those paths as separate directories.

## Why This Change Was Made

`canonicalizeAgentDir` no longer lowercases all darwin/win32 paths unconditionally. Collision identity uses a **shared** filesystem helper (`src/infra/path-case-sensitivity.ts`) that measures **child lookup semantics** on the closest existing directory (existing lettered entry first, temporary marker otherwise). Case-sensitive volumes keep case-distinct directories as distinct agent state homes; case-insensitive volumes still fold spellings that would share auth/session state. Trusted safe-bin path normalization uses the same helper so identity rules cannot diverge.

This also addresses ClawSweeper review on #105442: the first patch mirrored a parent-name case-swap probe that can misclassify absent paths at mount boundaries.

## User Impact

Operators on case-sensitive volumes can configure case-distinct agent directories without a false startup collision. Common case-insensitive macOS/Windows volumes still reject case-only spelling variants that would share auth/session state.

## Evidence

Verification host: local macOS (Crabbox bypass)

Focused tests:
```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/infra/path-case-sensitivity.test.ts \
  src/config/agent-dirs.test.ts \
  src/infra/exec-safe-bin-trust.test.ts \
  src/config/config.multi-agent-agentdir-validation.test.ts
# Test Files  4 passed (4)
# Tests  19 passed (19)
```

Path-scoped static:
```text
pnpm exec oxfmt --check src/infra/path-case-sensitivity.ts src/infra/path-case-sensitivity.test.ts src/config/agent-dirs.ts src/config/agent-dirs.test.ts src/infra/exec-safe-bin-trust.ts  # pass
pnpm exec oxlint src/infra/path-case-sensitivity.ts src/infra/path-case-sensitivity.test.ts src/config/agent-dirs.ts src/config/agent-dirs.test.ts src/infra/exec-safe-bin-trust.ts  # 0 warnings / 0 errors
git diff --check  # pass
```

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: case-distinct `agentDir` paths on a case-sensitive volume no longer raise a false duplicate-agentDir collision for **absent** nested paths (parent child-probe) and existing paths; identical paths still collide.
- Environment: local macOS arm64, branch `fix/105194-agent-dir-case-sensitive-collisions` (`0cab372fb`), Case-sensitive APFS sparseimage mounted at `/Volumes/OC105194Proof2`.
- Current-main contrast: unconditional darwin/win32 lowercasing maps case-distinct paths onto one collision key even when the volume stores them as distinct.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:
  1. `hdiutil create -size 32m -type SPARSE -fs "Case-sensitive APFS" -volname OC105194Proof2 … && hdiutil attach …`
  2. Create only the proof root (leave `AgentState` / `agentstate` **absent**)
  3. Call production `findDuplicateAgentDirs` + `pathCaseInsensitive` via `tsx`
  4. Create both case-distinct dirs and re-check; true shared path control
- Evidence after fix:
  ```text
  volume_child_case_insensitive false
  upper_exists false
  lower_exists false
  after_fix_absent_case_distinct_dupes 0
  after_fix_true_dupes 1 a,b
  after_fix_existing_case_distinct_dupes 0
  PROOF_OK
  ```
- Control check: identical `agentDir` strings still report one conflict for agents `a` and `b`.
- Observed result after fix: false collision gone for absent and existing case-distinct paths on case-sensitive volume; true duplicates still rejected; host tmp case folding covered by unit tests via shared helper.
- What was not tested: live Windows case-sensitive volume (same shared probe; not exercised on a Windows host here); full nested bind-mount mixed case-sensitivity lab (algorithm targets child semantics; unit tests cover absent parent walk + lettered-child and marker probes).

## AI disclosure

This fix was authored with AI assistance (Grok). Human operator ran the auto find→fix pipeline and review follow-up; verification commands and Real behavior proof were executed on the local macOS host.
